Using the formula for conditional probability, \(P(A|B) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)}\). In this context, \(A\) is the event that a student is in Year 10, and \(B\) is the event that a student prefers to travel by bus.

The number of students in Year 10 who prefer the bus is given as \(x\) in the table. The total number of students who prefer the bus is also given in the 'Total' column for 'Bus', which is 160.

Therefore, the probability that a randomly chosen student is in Year 10, given they prefer to travel by bus, is the number of Year 10 students who prefer the bus divided by the total number of students who prefer the bus.

This is \(\frac{\text{Number of Year 10 students who prefer bus}}{\text{Total number of students who prefer bus}} = \frac{x}{160}\).
